name: Desolation and Gray Canyons
agency: Bureau of Land Management, Price Field Office

camps.name: Gold Hole 1
camps.desc: Medium. Best at medium to high water.

camps.name: Gold Hole 2
camps.desc: Medium, with more shade than Gold Hole 1. Best at low to medium water. Dense vegetation.

camps.name: Lower Gold Hole
camps.desc: Large. Best at medium to high water.

camps.name: Rock House
camps.desc: Large. Hike up the wash to reach the sites; avoid dry washes because of flash floods.

camps.name: Opposite Stampede Flat
camps.desc: Very small after rockfall; fits a couple of people.

camps.name: Low-water sandbar
camps.desc: Occasionally available at low water.

camps.name: Fossil 1
camps.desc: Large. Best at medium to high water; hard to identify at high water.

camps.name: Fossil (Turtle) 2
camps.desc: Large. Same water notes as Fossil 1.

camps.name: Jack Creek
camps.desc: If it is taken, use a site farther downstream. Pull over quickly after entering the rapid.

camps.name: Lower Jack Creek
camps.desc: Morning shade.

camps.name: Mushroom
camps.desc: Small after a fallen cottonwood. Good for lunch and access to the petroglyphs.

camps.name: Upper Cedar Ridge
camps.desc: Large and very nice. A deep eddy good for swimming and kayak rolls. A cut bank to the beach at low water.

camps.name: Cedar Ridge 1
camps.desc: Very large.

camps.name: Cedar Ridge 2
camps.desc: Medium.

camps.name: Cedar Ridge 3
camps.desc: Medium.

camps.name: Flat Canyon
camps.desc: Large and very rocky at low water. Spring runoff can block the petroglyph hike. Arch hike up the canyon.

camps.name: Dripping Springs
camps.desc: Large.

camps.name: Fretwater
camps.desc: Large.

camps.name: Steer Ridge
camps.desc: Large.

camps.name: Surprise
camps.desc: Small, best at lower water.

camps.name: Calf Canyon
camps.desc: Medium.

camps.name: Snap Canyon
camps.desc: Medium.

camps.name: Three Canyon
camps.desc: Large, with a big beach at low water. A popular layover spot.

camps.name: Three Canyon 2
camps.desc: Medium. Best at medium to high water.

camps.name: Lower Three Canyon
camps.desc: Large.

camps.name: Lion Hollow
camps.desc: Large and sandy.

camps.name: Chandler
camps.desc: Small to medium.

camps.name: Trail Canyon 1
camps.desc: Large.

camps.name: Trail Canyon 2
camps.desc: Large.

camps.name: Above Bull Canyon
camps.desc: Large, sandy and shaded.

camps.name: Moonwater
camps.desc: Large.

camps.name: Red Point
camps.desc: Medium.

camps.name: Below Red Point
camps.desc: Large, with a sandy beach at medium to low water.

camps.name: Joe Hutch
camps.desc: Large. A tight pull-in that is hard at high water and rocky at low.

camps.name: McPherson
camps.desc: Large. Take the right channel around the island; sandy beach at low water.

camps.name: Above Wire Fence
camps.desc: Large and shady.

camps.name: Wire Fence 2
camps.desc: Medium and shady.

camps.name: Wire Fence 3
camps.desc: The largest Wire Fence camp with the least shade. Difficult pull-in at high water.

camps.name: Emergency camp
camps.desc: An option at lower water. No shade, and no viable camps until Range Creek.

camps.name: Lower Range Creek
camps.desc: Sunny, with a late sunset. The upper Range Creek camp is no longer viable after a large fire.

camps.name: Upper Rabbit Valley
camps.desc: Small. Only viable at medium to high water.

camps.name: Rabbit Valley
camps.desc: Large and sandy.

camps.name: Poverty
camps.desc: Large. Late sun and no shade.

camps.name: School Section
camps.desc: Large. Many bugs from the willows.

camps.name: Rattlesnake
camps.desc: Large, popular for swimming and very sunny. Hike up Rattlesnake Canyon.

camps.name: Nefertiti
camps.desc: Large. A pit toilet, picnic tables and road access, so expect other users.

camps.name: Upper Butler
camps.desc: Medium.

camps.name: Lower Butler
camps.desc: Medium.

camps.name: Sand Knolls
camps.desc: A big sandy beach with lots of shade, good at all levels.

camps.name: Short Canyon
camps.desc: About a mile above the take-out. Sandy beach at lower flows.

camps.name: Swasey's Beach
camps.desc: A BLM campground with 12 sites, fire rings, tables and an outhouse, $15 per night.

rapids.name: Jack Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Read and run, with rocks on the left at low water. Life jackets are mandatory from here to the take-out.

rapids.name: Dripping Springs Rapid
rapids.desc: Very shallow on the left at low water.

rapids.name: Upper Steer Ridge Rapid
rapids.desc: Scout from the left and run left of center. A sharp rock from 2022 rockfall sits in the left channel and wraps and tears boats; it is hard to see at medium flows.

rapids.name: Surprise Rapid
rapids.desc: A flat rock center-left can be a pour-over at high water; easily avoided on the right.

rapids.name: Upper Snap Canyon Rapid
rapids.desc: Large holes on the left at high water.

rapids.name: Moonwater Rapid
rapids.desc: Pass either side of the island at high water; use the left channel at medium to low.

rapids.name: Red Point Rapid
rapids.desc: A large hole on the left at high water. The common line threads boulders mid-rapid; watch the right.

rapids.name: Joe Hutch Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Read and run. A large hole above it at high water (over 30,000 cfs); run center or right of center.

rapids.name: Joe Hutch Canyon Rapid (Cow Swim)
rapids.desc: Scouting recommended. Run left of the main features, then move right near the bottom.

rapids.name: Wire Fence Rapid
rapids.desc: Right or left at high water; left at medium to low.

rapids.name: Three Fords Rapid
rapids.desc: Take the right channel for a fun wave train. Optional right-bank scout. A possible undercut wall on the right.

rapids.name: Range Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: At low to medium flow take the left channel above and run left.

rapids.name: Coal Creek Rapid
rapids.desc: Run right of center: left of the "thunderous" feature at the top and right of the large rock below.

rapids.name: Rattlesnake Rapid
rapids.desc: Pull left to avoid rocks on the right.

rapids.name: Stone Cabin Rapid
rapids.desc: Watch the boulders at the top.

hikes.name: Rock House Canyon petroglyphs
hikes.desc: Hike up the wash from camp. Do not touch the rock art.

hikes.name: Mushroom Rock petroglyphs
hikes.desc: Fremont rock art about a quarter mile from camp. Do not touch.

hikes.name: Flat Canyon petroglyphs
hikes.desc: A short walk to Fremont figures (arrived around 600 AD) and fainter Desert Archaic designs. A sacred site: stay on the trail.

hikes.name: Flat Canyon arch
hikes.desc: An arch hike up the canyon.

hikes.name: Rock Creek petroglyphs
hikes.desc: About 4 miles round trip. Stay on the upstream-side trail and do not cross the creek. A Fremont panel is at the mouth.

hikes.name: Three Canyons overlook
hikes.desc: An overlook and loop hike from the trailhead.

hikes.name: Range Creek
hikes.desc: A major Fremont site area with over 500 identified sites. Hiking is restricted and allowed only through the north gate, May through November.

hikes.name: Coal Creek overlook
hikes.desc: A hike from camp. Ute land ends above Coal Creek.

hikes.name: Rattlesnake Canyon
hikes.desc: A hike up the canyon from camp.

hikes.name: Desert Archaic petroglyphs
hikes.desc: A panel at the petroglyph parking. Watch for poison ivy and do not touch.

history: Rock art along the canyon was made by the Fremont people, who arrived around 600 AD, and earlier Desert Archaic people. The Range Creek side canyon has over 500 identified Fremont sites.
Curry Canyon is named for Flat Nose George Curry, a member of the Wild Bunch.
A cabin in Gray Canyon was used by dam surveyors in 1911.

rules.d: A physical copy of the permit and photo ID for the permit check. Rangers also check equipment and give a safety and etiquette orientation. Boat tags stay attached to the boats for the whole trip.

A properly sized Type I, III or V PFD approved for paddling or whitewater for each person. Children 12 and under wear theirs at all times, and everyone wears one from Jack Creek Rapid to the take-out.
A first-aid kit adequate for the group and for serious injuries, repair kits for the types of boats, and air pumps to reinflate after repairs.
A washable, leak-proof, reusable system sized for the group and trip length. Leaving solid human waste, or dumping it in vault toilets or trash at BLM facilities, is prohibited.
A durable metal fire pan at least 12 inches wide with a lip of at least 1.5 inches, carried on all trips even if you cook on stoves. A fire blanket under it is recommended.
An extra oar, paddle or motor, and a bail bucket or bilge pump unless self-bailing.
One spare paddle for 1 to 3 kayaks, canoes or inflatable kayaks, two for 4 to 6, three for 7 to 9, and so on.
A Type IV throwable or a rescue rope with at least 40 feet of line, and a whistle or horn.
Launch, travel within visual contact, and camp together. Boats may not be sent ahead to secure campsites.
Carry out charcoal, ash, garbage and human waste. Dishwater strainers are recommended. Keep side-canyon streams and springs free of soap.
Fires only in fire pans, and only with driftwood found along the banks and beaches.
Do not camp or build fires on public land within half a mile of the mouth of Rock Creek.
Do not remove, damage or destroy archaeological or historical resources. Do not touch rock art.
The trip must not be commercial: participants share actual costs equally and no one profits.
No upstream motorized travel except in emergencies, and slow, wakeless speed downstream.

landmarks.name: Sand Wash
landmarks.desc: Put-in. A primitive ramp and campground with first-come sites, plus "bug huts" that can be reserved and are recommended in spring and early summer. No running water; pack out trash.

landmarks.name: Undercut wall
landmarks.desc: An undercut rock wall that is hazardous to smaller craft.

landmarks.name: Steer Ridge scout parking
landmarks.desc: River-left parking for scouting the rapid, approved by the Ute Tribe.

landmarks.name: Rock Creek Ranch
landmarks.desc: A historic ranch. Do not camp on the property or within half a mile of the mouth of Rock Creek.

landmarks.name: Ouray Lodge and McPherson Ranch
landmarks.desc: River left, no access: Ute land.

landmarks.name: End of Desolation Canyon
landmarks.desc: Gray Canyon begins. The K-T boundary shows in the rock here.

landmarks.name: Curry Canyon
landmarks.desc: Named for Flat Nose George Curry, a Wild Bunch member.

landmarks.name: Historic cabin
landmarks.desc: Used by dam surveyors in 1911. River-left access is permitted from here to the take-out.

landmarks.name: Swasey's Beach
landmarks.desc: A BLM campground, formerly free camping.

permit.status: Required year-round · lottery May 1 to Sept 30

items.d: A permit is required year-round for travel on the Green River between Sand Wash and Nefertiti Rapid. Boating season is usually March through November; the river freezes from December through February.

items.t: Peak season lottery: May 1 to September 30
items.d: Apply on Recreation.gov from December 1 to January 31, one entry per person. Notifications are emailed on February 15. You must accept awarded dates by March 14, or they are cancelled on March 15.
Unawarded and cancelled dates become reservable on Recreation.gov on March 15 at 8 a.m. Mountain. Later cancellations reappear at random times.
Launches before May 1 and after September 30 are not in the lottery. They can be reserved starting December 1.
An alternate trip leader can be added only at the time of reservation.
Payment for everyone must be completed and the permit printed in the two weeks before launch, or the reservation is cancelled. No changes can be made once it is printed.
One report from 2023 put the success rate at about 6 percent.
$6, one time and non-refundable, plus $40 per person. The first person is paid at booking.
Reported at six groups per day in the peak season.
25 people or fewer, and no more than the number prepaid. Groups launching separately may not camp together if that puts more than 25 people at one campsite.
At least 3 and at most 9 calendar days.
Pets are prohibited year-round on Desolation and Gray Canyons.
Cancel more than 30 days before launch for a refund of everything but the $6. There is no refund within 30 days, or for reducing the group. Permits cannot be transferred or sold.

The east bank from Sand Wash to Coal Creek is Ute Tribal land. All activity there has been prohibited since September 2018: no landing, no visiting sites, no camping, no hiking. Plan every camp on river right, which is BLM land.
River-left access is permitted from below Coal Creek to the take-out.
